ratings_why.fun: The curve has a real shape: sticky 2/2s win early, Mixer and Bufo grow the board mid-game, and Crest, Hesketh and Zilvinas give a capstone worth climbing to.
ratings_why.distinct: Going limp and rising together at the Curtain Call is a fresh fight pattern, though the Death Scene engine still reads like a Deathrattle tribe.

verdict_why: v2 closed the loops and unclear cards; what is left is hot multiplier stacking for the owner to balance, not a fix.

points.text: Growth depends on units going down, so a clean win grows little. Coronella, Eft and Saucers cover it; one more Tier 2 shop-side trigger would smooth the early curve.
Household Guardian's Saucer on Sir Hesketh under Old Crest is a full board rehearsal every turn. A strong, legible late plan; keep it and let the owner tune numbers.
Born-in-the-Wings Hatchling is a weak early body that only grows Attack. Health too (+1/+1 per play dead) would let it last into the mid-game it is seeding.
The Brothers Berus's 'at most two each time he goes down' doesn't cover scenes triggered by Sir Hesketh or Eft. The empty-slot fizzle bounds it, but a line in the text would help.

standouts.why: Bufo turns every limp unit into a bigger second act; the cleanest mid-game engine in the tribe.
Coronella makes deaths happen on your schedule and opens the seating puzzle.
Zilvinas is a true capstone: more lives and more Curtain Calls for the comp built to reach it.

weakest.why: Attack-only growth on a 1/2 body that dies early; a seed that rarely sprouts.
Plain gold drip capped at 2; does its job but adds no decisions.
Shed-Skin Dresser is a 2/5 body with a one-off grant; filler next to the Tier 3 engines.

flags.note: Sir Hesketh with Old Crest and the Millpond Maid multiplies every scene 4x or more, in fight and in the shop.
Old Crest working while recruiting doubles every Eft and Saucer rehearsal; golden Crest triples it.
Repeated Berus scenes from Hesketh and Crest can destroy several big enemies a fight; positional counterplay only.
